text.en: Meena saw a methane flame in the school lab. "Carbon compounds burn well," said her teacher.

Organic compounds have special characteristics such as covalent bonding, low melting points and the ability to burn. They are classified by the carbon chain as open-chain or acyclic and closed-chain or cyclic compounds. Hydrocarbons are compounds of carbon and hydrogen only, and they are saturated alkanes or unsaturated alkenes and alkynes.
Bromine water test: alkenes decolourise bromine water, but alkanes do not. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group where each member differs from the next by a CH2 group. Members have similar chemical properties and gradually changing physical properties.
IUPAC nomenclature gives every organic compound a systematic name, with a root word for the number of carbons, a prefix and a suffix for the functional group. The rules for naming include choosing the longest chain, numbering it and naming the substituents.

problem.en: What is the difference between two neighbouring members of a homologous series?

text.en: They differ by one carbon and its hydrogens.

prompt.en: A friend says Alkanes decolourise bromine water. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Alkanes are saturated and do not.

points.en: Hydrocarbons have only C and H.
A homologous series differs by CH2.
